blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings rose from 86 in June to 94 in October (+9.3%), and it took 12.0% of the city’s 357 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings was 0 in June and 2 in October, too few (under 3) to call a rise or fall, and it took 0.0% of the city’s 694 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Brookswood for detached houses in June, August, September (a buyers’ best bet).

items.t: Brookswood is a sub-area of the Township of Langley, BC, inside the Brookswood-Fernridge community area; the Township plan name is the Brookswood-Fernridge Community Plan, covering the Booth, Fernridge and Rinn neighbourhoods.

Plan-area study boundaries (Township commercial market demand study for Booth, Fernridge and Rinn): bounded to the west by 196 Street, to the north by 33A Avenue, 200 Street, 36 Avenue, 208 Street and 43 Avenue, to the east by Murray Creek, 40 Avenue, 210 Street and 208 Street, and to the south by 20 Avenue, 198 Street and 16 Avenue.

Brookswood's detached ratio of 7% is the lowest published detached ratio in the Langley set that month, and its detached inventory of 98 is the second-largest in the set, behind Willoughby Heights at 100. SnapStats publishes medians at community level only (Langley = City + Township combined). Combined-Langley context only (not Brookswood figures): Detached median $1,345,000; Condos & Townhomes median $611,000.

Parks and services: the Township lists Brookswood Park, Brookswood Skateboard Park, Noel Booth Community Park, Bell Park, Dale Ball Passive Park, East Brookswood Park, Highpoint Park, Rees-Callard Natural Park and Wiser Natural Area among Brookswood/Fernridge parks; George Preston Recreation Centre is at 20699 42 Avenue; Brookswood Library (Fraser Valley Regional Library) is at 20045 40 Avenue. Health care: Langley Memorial Hospital, 22051 Fraser Highway, is the nearest hospital confirmed on a health authority source; the nearest Urgent and Primary Care Centre is the Langley UPCC, 202 - 20434 64th Avenue.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Brookswood Guide

items.t: Township plans and zoning: the Brookswood-Fernridge Community Plan covers the area, with Booth, Fernridge and Rinn Neighbourhood Plans under it; the Township states the plan allows previously undeveloped areas to grow while protecting trees and watercourses. Zoning is Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw 1987 No. 2500: Section 110.1 in Township council reports sets SR-1 minimum lot area 3,716 m² (40 m frontage), SR-2 minimum 8,094 m² (45 m) and SR-3 minimum 1,765 m² (27.45 m).

SSMUH — Township Bylaw 6020: Zoning Amendment Bylaw 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024) allows 3 units on eligible lots of 280 m² or smaller, 4 units on larger eligible lots up to 4,050 m²; lots over 4,050 m² are ineligible. The Township has no six-unit tier.

Secondary suites and coach houses (Township): the Township caps a secondary suite at 120 m² maximum gross floor area (Zoning Bylaw No. 2500, s. 102). A coach house in the Township is a fee-simple second unit under Zoning Bylaw 2500 s. 102; it is not strata and not a condo.

Pad rent (parks): where a Brookswood purchase is a park home, pad rent is governed by the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act, not the Strata Property Act: the rent increase limit for manufactured home site tenancies is 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026 and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027, with 3 full months' notice and one increase per 12 months.

blocks.text: Good to know about Brookswood Guide

items.t: The "condo" shelf here is two listings deep.

Three of the area's best-known "communities" are pad-rental parks, not strata. Cedar Creek Estates (3031 200 St), Fernridge Park (20071 24 Ave) and Pineridge (2270 196 St) all record leasehold non-strata tenure in listings and publish 55+ rules — park rules under a tenancy act, with pad rent under the MHPTA increase formula (2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026; 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027), not strata fees under a Form B.
Cedar Lane is not Cedar Creek, and neither status should be borrowed. None is counted anywhere.
The school locator cannot place the secondary school's own address. A Brookswood school claim made without a locator run for the exact address is a guess.
The guide feed and the board count different Brookswoods. The two sources measure different sets at different moments, and neither should be quoted as the other.
Zoning minimums, not averages, frame Brookswood lots. Section 110.1 of Bylaw 2500 in Township council reports runs SR-3 at a 1,765 m² minimum up to SR-2 at 8,094 m².

blocks.text: Lots and land in Brookswood Langley
What trades here

items.t: Fee-simple lots — the default form: Brookswood's documented housing form is single-family housing — urban lots in the established streets and larger rural and acreage parcels under the suburban and rural zones. A fee-simple lot carries no strata corporation, no Form B and no strata fees.

Lot character, only: zones named in Township notices for the area include Suburban Residential SR-1, SR-2 and SR-3 and Rural Zone RU-2; read from Bylaw 2500 Section 110.1 in Township council reports, SR-1 minimum lot area is 3,716 m² (frontage 40 m), SR-2 is 8,094 m² (45 m) and SR-3 is 1,765 m² (27.45 m). Brookswood is known locally for larger treed lots — that is a characterization, not a measured average.

Named developer project, documented as built-form context, never as land: Brookswood Estates, by Foxridge Homes — a detached single-family developer project named from a developer source; the developer page states no civic address.
ALR vs non-ALR split: much of the Township's land is in the Agricultural Land Reserve. No Brookswood ALR share is stated.
The condos homes count 0 apartment condos for this area and the 55-plus home counts 0 verified 55+ strata.
No assembly site is carried as inventory.
The one Brookswood presale is Bromley, a townhouse presale (above), not a lot offering.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Brookswood Langley

items.t: Zoning — Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw 2500: Community plan: the Brookswood-Fernridge Community Plan covers Brookswood-Fernridge, with Booth, Fernridge and Rinn Neighbourhood Plans under it; the Township states the plan allows previously undeveloped areas to grow while protecting trees and watercourses. City of Langley bylaws do not apply here.
SSMUH — Township Bylaw 6020 (adopted Nov 18, 2024): Eligibility and servicing are per-lot — confirm with the Township.

Subdivision and servicing — Township Bylaw 5382 (2019): all subdivisions must be approved by the Approving Officer under the Land Title Act, through application, review, decision, conditions, final approval and registration; servicing is determined under Bylaw 5382.

ALR block: subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)). Caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Check a parcel in GeoSource / on the ALC maps.

Zoning minimums, not averages, frame Brookswood lots (Township council report, June 10, 2024). Section 110.1 of Bylaw 2500 runs SR-3 at a 1,765 m² minimum up to SR-2 at 8,094 m².
The school locator cannot place the secondary school's own address (Nov 1, 2026). A Brookswood school claim made without a locator run for the exact address is a guess.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Brookswood
What trades here

items.t: Tenure — fee-simple is the default: Brookswood's documented housing form is single-family housing — urban lots in the established streets and larger rural and acreage parcels under the suburban and rural zones — plus Cedar Creek Manufactured Home Park at 3031 - 200 Street, designated Manufactured Home Park in the plan (a pad-rental park, not owned land).
Brookswood Estates, by Foxridge Homes — a detached single-family developer project named from a developer source; the developer page states no civic address.

Lot character — only: zoning named in Township notices for the area includes Suburban Residential SR-1, SR-2 and SR-3 and Rural Zone RU-2; under Bylaw 2500 s.110.1, SR-1 minimum lot area is 3,716 m², SR-2 is 8,094 m² and SR-3 is 1,765 m².

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Brookswood

items.t: Transit: TransLink routes 531, 561 and 563 serve 200 Street at 37A Avenue, connecting to Langley Centre; no SkyTrain or West Coast Express station is in Brookswood.
How people search for it: "Brookswood," "Brookswood Langley," "Brookswood-Fernridge," and Booth, Fernridge and Rinn.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Brookswood

items.t: Strata block (bare-land strata parcels): Form B within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions). A fee-simple lot carries none of this.

Water and septic: the provincial GWELLS registry holds recorded wells (older wells may not appear); a home not connected to a community sewer must use an onsite sewage system complying with the Sewerage System Regulation, designed and installed by an Authorized Person (Fraser Health).

blocks.text: Good to know about Brookswood

items.t: SSMUH eligibility in Brookswood is a servicing map, not a slogan (Township council report, June 10, 2024). The Township's own estimate puts Brookswood at ~15% of single-family/duplex lots eligible for 3–4 units, against ~99% in Walnut Grove — because eligibility follows existing municipal water and sewer.

A strata plan is a subdivision in the ALR — even with no building (ALC Information Bulletin 09). Filing a bare-land strata plan on reserve land triggers the same ALC permission requirement as a conventional subdivision.
The R-CL maximum is a LOT-area cap, not a floor-area cap (Bylaw 2500 s.403). R-CL runs 220 m² minimum lot area to 464.5 m² maximum lot area; a "355 m²" figure appears nowhere in the bylaw.

faq.a: No. Township SSMUH under Bylaw 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024) allows 3 units on eligible lots of 280 m² or smaller and 4 units on larger eligible lots up to 4,050 m². A lot also needs municipal water and sewer to qualify, and some Brookswood lots are still on septic, so confirm servicing with the Township.

faq.a: No — the November 24, 2022 voiding applies to strata rental-restriction bylaws. Park rules sit under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act and the park's own rules and tenancy agreement; a park's 55+ and no-rentals lines in listings (Fernridge Park's listing states pets and rentals are not permitted, with park manager approval required) are listing-stated park rules to confirm with the park, not void strata bylaws.
faq.q: The parks say 55+ and no rentals. Are those rules void like strata rules?

faq.a: No. Township SSMUH under Bylaw 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024) allows 3 units on lots up to 280 m² and 4 units on lots up to 4,050 m², so six as-of-right units on a Brookswood lot is not possible. Lots over 4,050 m² are not eligible for the SSMUH tiers, and eligible lots need municipal water and sewer and must sit outside a Transit-Oriented Area.
faq.q: Can I put six units on a Brookswood house lot?

faq.a: In a pad-rental park, no: you own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad — the park owns the land, and your right to the site is the assigned pad tenancy under the MHPTA.
faq.q: Do I own the land in a Brookswood park?

faq.a: Confirm its status and rules with the park, in writing, before treating it as stock.
faq.q: What about Cedar Lane Park at 2305 200 St — is it a third option?

faq.a: Per its listing text it is a custom home with two lower-level suites — a single house with suites, not a duplex in either legal form on any primary source here. Township suites are capped at 120 m², and suite legality is a per-parcel check.
faq.q: The house at 20061 27 Avenue has two suites — is it a duplex?

faq.a: No — per the disk they are pad-rental leasehold non-strata parks, documented at their Brookswood mobile homes. You would own the home as a chattel and rent the pad; you would not own land, and the mhpta — not the Strata Property Act — governs.
faq.q: Are Cedar Creek Estates or Fernridge Park bare-land strata?
